title: Satyakama's four teachers
hookLine: sent off with four hundred thin cows, Satyakama is taught by the herd's bull, the evening fire, a swan and a diving bird
last: SATYA: SATYA: TRUTH IS THE QUALIFICATION.

lines: ALONE IN THE FOREST FOR YEARS.
cards: Satyakama has been accepted. You'd expect his first lesson to be a verse, a chant, a teaching by the fire. Instead his teacher picks out four hundred cows, thin and weak, and says: look after these.
Satyakama doesn't complain. I won't come back, he says, until they're a thousand. He drives them off into the forest and stays away for years.
No teacher. No books. Just cows, grass and sky.
And out there, alone, the lessons start arriving, from teachers nobody would have chosen.

teach.b: When the herd reaches a thousand, the bull speaks. Satyakama, we're a thousand now. Take us home, and let me tell you one quarter of Brahman, the great reality.
The bull names the four directions, east, west, south, north, and calls that quarter the shining. The fire, it says, will tell him the next.

teach.h: THE FIRE, THE SWAN, THE DIVING BIRD.
teach.b: That evening Satyakama lights the fire and pens the cows, and the fire speaks: earth, the air between, the sky, the ocean. That quarter is the endless. The next evening a swan flies down: fire, sun, moon, lightning.
The luminous. The evening after, a diving water bird: breath, eye, ear, mind. The quarter that has a home.
Four teachers, four quarters: the directions, the worlds, the lights, and his own body.

teach.h: YOUR FACE SHINES. WHO TAUGHT YOU?
teach.b: He reaches his teacher's house, and the teacher looks at him and says: your face shines like someone who knows Brahman. Who taught you? Beings other than people, Satyakama answers.
But please, teach me yourself. His teacher does, and the text says nothing was left out.
That's the teaching: Brahman, the one reality, isn't only at the altar. It shines in the directions, the worlds, the lights, and in your own breath and eyes.
Hindus live that when they greet the rising sun, light a lamp at dusk, or bow to a river. And look back at the week: om, breath, a dogs' chant, a boy's truth, and now a herd at evening.
Each day, the Chandogya found Brahman somewhere new.

how: Many Hindus greet the rising sun with folded hands or an offering of water, light a lamp at dusk and bow to rivers; teachers tell Satyakama's story to show that Brahman can be met anywhere, and that a teacher still completes the learning.

o: Satyakama's first teacher, who names the four directions
the animal the teacher rides out to the forest
a sign that the herd has reached a thousand

games.q: who taught which quarter — tap the pairs.

s: Satyakama's teacher sent him off with a thousand cows
four hundred thin, weak cows. Satyakama vowed not to return until they were a thousand.
Satyakama asks his teacher to teach him anyway
even after the bull, fire, swan and bird, he asks to hear it from his teacher, and nothing is left out.
the teacher says Satyakama's face shines like a knower of Brahman
he can see it before Satyakama says a word.

games.q: you're Satyakama, home with a thousand cows. a bull, a fire, a swan and a bird have taught you. your teacher asks who taught you. what do you do next?
o: say you need no teacher now.
tell him the truth, and ask him to teach you himself.
claim you figured it all out alone.
games.why: he says: beings other than people. then he asks his teacher to teach him anyway, and the teacher does, leaving nothing out.

practice: Notice the direction you're facing and the ones behind and beside you, the bull's quarter; then the ground and the air above it, the fire's; then whatever light is around you, the swan's.
Come home to your breath, your eyes, your ears and your mind, the diving bird's. No need to hear any voices; just let each one be a teacher for a few breaths.

wordCard.voice: The bull. The first of Satyakama's four unlikely teachers, who names the four directions as the shining quarter of Brahman.

orig.note: Sanskrit haṃsa: swan or wild goose, the third of Satyakama's teachers.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole world teaches Brahman. Even a bull, a swan and an evening fire. Week one of year two, done.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 4.5–4.8 (the bull, the fire, the swan, the diving bird)
Chandogya Upanishad 4.9 (your face shines; nothing left out)
